Our story

Twenty-five years in, still led by the founder.

The work has changed shape many times. Who leads it has not.

Chapter 01

1999/ 04
One founder. One continuous line.
  1. 01Chapter 011999

    1999

    Code was the foundation

    With credentials in Computer Science and Computer Information Systems, Keisha began coding when websites were still built largely by hand in HTML. She founded EVOBRAND Marketing in 1999 to bring that technical foundation to brand and digital work.

  2. 02Chapter 022003

    2003

    Early WordPress contributor

    Keisha was one of the first contributors to WordPress, helping shape the open-source platform during its earliest years.

  3. 03Chapter 032010

    2010

    EVOBRAND Concepts

    After years of building across the Dallas–Fort Worth area, the business became EVOBRAND Concepts LLC in 2010 and expanded its work across strategy, design, and development.

  4. 04Chapter 04Today

    Today

    Animation, systems, and AI

    Keisha’s longtime passion for animation now shapes how she brings digital ideas to life. Today, she enjoys implementing AI throughout her workflows while continuing to lead EVOBRAND’s strategy, design, development, and platform work.

How we work

Four promises we keep on every project.

  • Plain answers

    Clear scope, honest timelines, and written decisions. You always know where the project stands.

  • One accountable lead

    The person who scopes the work stays on it through launch and after.

  • Built to be run

    We design systems your staff can operate after we hand them over, not just launch.

  • Accountable

    Every project starts with agreed outcomes, and we report against them.

Leadership

Keisha Solomon, Founder.

Keisha has led the business since 1999 and leads every EVOBRAND engagement directly.

Keisha founded the company as EVOBRAND Marketing and has spent more than 25 years building brands, websites, and digital platforms for government agencies, corporations, and nonprofits. Under her leadership, EVOBRAND built ChamberCore, which runs chambers of commerce, and EVOGovCon, which connects skilled trade workers and small businesses with government prime contractors.
